title: A hunt target in few paragraphs
statement: A target the learner hunts for to locate evidence, such as a word, must pick out at most two of the paragraphs searched, since a target found everywhere teaches nothing.
example: On approved lessons hunt targets clustered at one paragraph and a known defect at four, so the check fails a target found in three or more.
detail: A Grade 3 reading project wrote extra content checkers after eleven defects survived a fully green check suite, seven of them mechanically checkable. Its key-integrity checker requires a hunt target to land in at most 2 of the paragraphs the child is actually searching, counting only the paragraph openings the hunt shows and asks the child to tap, not the whole passage. The checker prints a spread table so the threshold can be seen: good lessons cluster at 1 and the defect at 4, and the check fails at 3 or more.
against: The recorded baseline still holds one key-spread finding on an approved lesson (`grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/STATE.md`, line 110) that the sources read never adjudicate, and the threshold was calibrated only on this course's lessons. A later ruling in the same project dropped keyword hunting from the finding procedure, because many texts have no clean keyword to hunt for (`grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/03-INSTRUCTION-DESIGN.md`, lines 68-69).

evidence.quote: KEY-SPREAD      a hunt target must land in at most 2 of the paragraphs the child is actually searching. A target in many paragraphs points everywhere and teaches nothing.

A hunt question glows a handful of paragraph openings (`hunt.first_lines`) and asks the child to tap one. That glowing set — not the whole chapter — is the search space, so it is the honest denominator.
The spread table makes the threshold visible and defensible rather than arbitrary: you can see the good lessons cluster at 1 and the defect at 4.
**Green is the floor, not the bar.** On 2026-08-21 eleven defects survived a fully green `npm run check`, and seven of them were mechanically checkable — nobody had written the check.
In L14's last task, the word the child is asked to hunt for is "Toad". It appears in thirteen of the paragraphs they are searching, so it points everywhere at once.
"hunt" (keyword spotting) was ruled out 2026-08-25 because many texts have no clean keyword to hunt for
